exam: 2008 AP Chemistry MCQ · Version indicated in source
text:
Questions 7-9 refer to the following pure
substances, which are gases at 25°C and 1
atmosphere.

     (A)  NH3 (g)
      (B)  BH3 (g)
      (C)  H2 (g)
     (D)  H2S (g)
      (E)  HBr (g)

8.  Is a strong electrolyte in aqueous solution

crop.note: Compared complete individual crop for Question 8 against original 2008 source page. Common context is linked via stimulus-2008-mcq-7-9-page31; individual stem and choices are separate and complete.

candidates.name: Strong versus weak acids and bases
candidates.definition: Distinguishing strong acids and bases (complete ionization) from weak ones (partial ionization), and separating acid strength from acid concentration.
candidates.include: Tag when an acid or base must be classified as strong or weak, or its extent of ionization represented or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag structure-based strength explanations (tag acid-strength-structure) or Ka calculations (tag weak-acid-equilibrium).

candidates.name: Brønsted-Lowry acids, bases and conjugate pairs
candidates.definition: Identifying proton donors and acceptors in a reaction, writing conjugate acid-base pairs, and recognizing amphiprotic species such as water.
candidates.include: Tag when acids, bases or conjugate pairs must be identified, or a proton-transfer equation written.
candidates.exclude: Lewis acid-base theory is not assessed.

candidates.name: Molecular structure and acid strength
candidates.definition: Explaining relative acid strength from bond polarity and strength, electronegativity of nearby atoms (oxyacids, inductive effects), and stabilization of the conjugate base by resonance or charge.
candidates.include: Tag when acid strengths must be ranked or explained from molecular structure.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag strength ranking from given Ka values only (tag weak-acid-equilibrium).

candidates.name: Weak acid and base equilibria (Ka, Kb)
candidates.definition: Writing Ka and Kb expressions, calculating pH or K for weak acid and base solutions, percent ionization, and Ka·Kb = Kw for conjugates.
candidates.include: Tag when Ka, Kb, percent ionization or the pH of a weak acid or base solution must be used or calculated.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag buffer pH calculations (tag henderson-hasselbalch) or titration-curve reading (tag titration-curves).
